## 2024-11-02 - Fix XSS in QR Code Generation
**Vulnerability:** The application was using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to render a QR code SVG generated by `qrcode-generator`. While `qrcode-generator` is generally safe, the `link` variable passed to `qr.addData(link)` could potentially contain malicious input if not strictly validated or if the QR library doesn't adequately escape it within the SVG context. Using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is inherently risky when dealing with dynamic data.
**Learning:** Rendering dynamically generated SVGs with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` can open XSS vectors if the library or the data source is not perfectly safe. `qrcode-generator` provides `createDataURL()` which can be safely rendered using a standard `<img>` tag without opening up DOM-based XSS vulnerabilities.
**Prevention:** Avoid `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` whenever possible. When generating images or QR codes from dynamic data, use data URLs (e.g., `createDataURL()`) and render them securely via `<img>` tags.
